chunks: That Abū al-Ḥasan al-Thānī, peace be upon him, said:
"Slaughtering the game, eating it, and paying the expiation is more beloved to me than carrion."

key_terms.الْمَيْتَةِ: carrion, an animal not slaughtered properly
key_terms.وَيَفْدِي: and pays the expiation or ransom due
key_terms.يَذْبَحُ: slaughters in the legally prescribed manner

ai.seo_question: For a muhrim who kills game, is eating it with expiation preferable to eating carrion?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal preference in the case of a muhrim who has taken game: slaughtering the animal, eating it, and then paying the required expiation is preferable to eating carrion. It reflects a jurisprudential ruling connected to hajj and the laws of prohibited hunting in ihram.
